solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tree remained sound with early treatment

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: sound tells us to take a word as it is spoken, not as it is written

parts.note: remained means stayed

explanation.surface: A tree stayed standing while someone got prompt medical help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' marks a homophone: the word for remained is spoken, and its sound-alike meaning sober is what is written.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the emergency care given right away, before a doctor arrives.

clue.text: Prophet is first-class, given a head start

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as AI

indicators.note: start asks for the first letter of the word head

explanation.surface: A holy man is top-rate and gets a lead over the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI, the one standing as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is one of the major prophets of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Remains to give support

definitions.meaning: to remain somewhere is to linger there without leaving
props, ropes or corset stiffeners that hold something up

explanation.definitionFit: Stays means remains as a verb, and stays are supports such as a mast's ropes or corset bones.

clue.text: Totaliser beaten by great logician

indicators.note: beaten suggests the letters have been knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A betting machine is outdone by a great thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle, the Greek philosopher, founded formal logic.

clue.text: It's most expensive, darling

definitions.meaning: the superlative of dear in the sense of costly
a term of endearment for a loved one

explanation.definitionFit: Dear means both costly and beloved, so its superlative serves as both a price word and an endearment.

clue.text: To hush an upset baby is rather mean

parts.note: SH is the sound made to hush someone

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the next word are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Telling an upset infant to be quiet is a bit unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like it describes the baby's mood, but it signals the rearrangement; 'rather mean' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby treatment is mean and ungenerous, a near synonym for being rather mean.

clue.text: Start court proceedings

parts.note: reads as beginning a legal case, but the court is a tennis court where each point begins with a delivery

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a serve is the stroke that starts each point played on court.

clue.text: Bill is not keen about raising it

indicators.note: about means one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: adverse means opposed, not keen on something

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the word it is read upwards

explanation.surface: Bill is reluctant to bring the subject up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' reverses the pronoun in a down clue. 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is the verb, as in to bill a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To bill something is to publicise it on posters, which is to advertise it.

clue.text: Daring kind of chap that makes the headlines

parts.note: daring means bold
a type is a kind of person, as in 'he's not my type'

explanation.surface: A daring sort of fellow ends up in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy bold type is the printing used for newspaper headlines.

clue.text: Where in Africa one backs law to some degree

indicators.note: backs means the next piece stands behind the one before it

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone supports the law to a certain extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' means stands behind: the numeral one comes after the law. 'to some degree' supplies a university degree in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked country in south-east Africa.

clue.text: Artist set back by competitors' entries

indicators.note: set back means the letters of the word artist's abbreviation are reversed

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
competitors are rivals

explanation.surface: A painter is held up by the submissions of other contestants.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrivals are those who enter or come in, so entries in the sense of people arriving.

clue.text: A recorder may accept this involved test case

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tape machine takes on a complicated legal test case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape recorder takes a cassette, the tape cartridge that slots into it.

clue.text: Mistakes put back a sailor in time

indicators.note: in means the sailor goes inside the period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: put back means the word for a sailor is reversed

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Errors set a seaman back in his timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns TAR into RAT, placed in ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed printing mistakes; the word is Latin plural for errors.

clue.text: Oscar's tiptop variety of bar snack

indicators.note: variety of suggests a different arrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Oscar's excellent range of pub nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of OSCARS TIPTOP, the S included, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Packets of potato crisps are a staple snack sold in British pubs; crisps are what Americans call chips.

clue.text: Dine with Ralph, prepared to flirt

indicators.note: prepared suggests the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Eat with Ralph, ready to make advances.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to flirt or have casual affairs with women.

clue.text: Drink most commonly sold in bars

definitions.meaning: describes the confectionery that is usually sold as slabs rather than in pubs

explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate is both a hot drink and a sweet usually sold in bars.

clue.text: The dog on the line is mine

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a collie is a breed of dog
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: The dog on the railway track belongs to me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive but is a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal mine with its buildings.

clue.text: Occasion when victory must be obtained quickly?

definitions.text: Occasion when victory must be obtained quickly?

parts.words: Occasion when victory must be obtained quickly?
parts.note: reads as a match where a draw or defeat is not allowed, but describes any urgent hurry

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means there is urgency, while the clue reads it literally as a moment when losing is ruled out.

clue.text: Portentous doctor lifted one with commonsense

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor
I is the Roman numeral for one
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: A gloomy medic picked up someone sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous and portentous both mean foreboding, hinting at something bad to come.

clue.text: Go off to find another partner

definitions.meaning: to take oneself off somewhere, as in withdrawing to the lounge

explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is to go there, and re-pair splits as pairing up again.

clue.text: In factory one is easily modified

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the factory word

parts.note: a plant is a factory
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone working at a factory is easily swayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant means flexible, easily bent or influenced.

clue.text: Upset about work, drinks!

indicators.note: about means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: upset read as set up, the word set written upwards in a down clue
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Distressed about the job, one hits the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' is read as set up, the word set written upwards in this down clue, and wraps round the abbreviation for a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is an old word meaning to drink heavily, so topes means drinks.

clue.text: Ladies to move far from others

indicators.note: move suggests the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Women are to relocate somewhere remote.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means remote, set apart from other people or places.

clue.text: Head of Harrow?

parts.note: reads as the headmaster of Harrow School, but asks for the name of the first letter of the word Harrow

explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school, so Head suggests its headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of Harrow is H, and the spelt-out name of that letter is the answer.

clue.text: Senior counsel competent enough to approach the case in stages

parts.note: the lead is the senior barrister in a case
up to a task means competent enough for it

explanation.surface: A barrister qualified to argue a case step by step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' after 'competent enough' is a link word; the legal surface hides the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead up to something is to approach it gradually, step by step.

clue.text: Lost, as a dog may be

definitions.meaning: gone missing, off the right path
a dog may be a stray, heard as one word

explanation.definitionFit: Astray means lost, and run together it is how a homeless dog is described.

clue.text: Starting cold, take syrup mixture in sunny island

indicators.note: starting asks for the first letter of the word cold
mixture says the letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: With a cold coming on, take cough syrup on a Mediterranean holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is a Mediterranean island known for its hot sunny climate.

clue.text: The lamb's tender

parts.note: reads as meat being soft, but tender means one who tends a flock

explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd is the person who tends sheep and lambs.
